FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Dyes Intermediate Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. o-Chioro p-nitro aniline is an important intermediate used in the manufacture of azo dyes. It is represented by the following formula:

Ortho-Chloro Para-Nitro Aniline (OCPNA) Molecular Mass = 172.5 [CAS Registry No. 121-87-9] The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex C.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

METHOD A-1 PRINCIPLE

OF TEST FOR ASSAY OF ORTHO-CHLORO

A known mass of the sample is dissolved in concentrated sulphuric acid, re-precipitated in finely divided form by dilution and titrated against standard sodium nitrite solution in presence of hydrochloric acid. A-2 PROCEDURE A-2.1 Weigh accurately weighing bottle (W,). about lg of sample in

A-2.2 Transfer the substance into one litre beaker and reweigh the weighing bottle (Wz). A-2.3 (W, � IVz) gives taken = M the mass of the sample

A-2.4 Add 10 ml of cone sulphuric acid and make it homogeneous by stirring. A-2.5 Add 20 ml of cone hydrochloric A-2.6 Add 1g of potassium bromide. I acid.

Add ice ~nd cold water to bring the temperature between O to 5 C and adjust the volume about to 700 ml to get clear endpoint. The endpoint is indicated by appearance of blue colour on starch iodide paper. A-2.8 Calculate the percentage purity of OCPNA by following formula: V X N X 17.25 M

DETERMINATION 0F3,4 DICHLORO NITRO BENZENE 2,6 DICHLORO-4-NITROANILINE AND 4-NITROANILINE B-O GENERAL For details of TLC test method, reference maybe made to IS 5299. B-1 APPARATUS AND CHEMICALS B-3 SPOTTING, ANALYSIS

(3,4 DCNB), CONTENTS AND

DEVELOPING

B-1.1 Aluminium foils pre-coated with silica gel, calibrated syringe, Hair drier, Development chamber, UV cabinet, iodine chamber. 4-Nitroaniline standard sample, 3,4 DCNB standard sample, 2,6 Dichloro-4nitroaniline standard sample, 4-nitroaniline, toluene, chloroform, Ammonia solution (sp. gravity 0.91,25 percent m/m). B-2 PREPARATION OF STOCK SOLUTIONS

B-3.1 Spot 2,4,6,8,10 ml of stock solution. These spots are corresponding to 0.1 percent, 0.2 percent, 0.3 percent, 0.4 percent and 0.5 percent of standard DCNB respectively. Spot 10 ml of sample solution also. Dry the spots with hair drier. B-3.2 Develop the plate in toluene solvent saturated with ammonia. Dry the plate and observe the plate in W cabinet at 254 nm. B-3.3 Compare the intensity of DCNB spots of standard DCNB solutions with the spots at same Rf value produced by the sample. B-3.4 DCNB can be quantitatively determined up to 0.5 percent in sample by comparing the colour intensities. For 0.5 percent to 2 percent DCNB content spot 2,4,6,8 ml of standard DCNB along with 2 ml of sample solution. Repeat the process. The standard DCNB spots corresponds to 0.5 percent, 1 percent, 1.5 percent and 2 percent DCNB respectively. B-3.5 Similarly, determine the percentage of 2,6 dichloro-4-nitroaniline and 4-nitroaniline present.

B-2.1 Weigh exactly 0.1 g of standard 3,4 DCNB. Make the volume to 100 ml using chloroform. Strength ofthis solution is 1 ml = 1 mg of DCNB (Use this as a stock solution). B-2.2 Take 5 ml of above stock solution and dilute it to 100 ml with chloroform and use for spotting. B-2.3 Similarly, prepare standard sample solutions of 2,6 Dichloro-4-nitroaniline and 4-nitroaniline. B-2.4 Then prepare sample solution of 100 ml in chloroform from 0.1 g sample. If insoluble matter is present, filter it and use.
